messages:
mika: FYI bringing up verne32b-int4 on a single 80GB A100 (dedicated). Intermittent OOMs during warmup/generation with batch=4 and max_new_tokens=1024. Logs point to kv cache expansion failures, looks like fragmentation rather than steady-state allocation.
infra-bot: deploy/canary started for verne32b-int4 on node gpu-dedicated-17 (canary id: c-1845123456)
takashi: @mika can you paste the exact OOM trace? int4 cuts model params but kv cache still scales with sequence length. For big max_new_tokens we often need to lower defaults or disable prefetch.
mika: log excerpt:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.2 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 70.10 GiB already allocated; 2.60 GiB free; 40.00 GiB reserved in allocator)
  at runtime/inference/kv_cache.cpp:342 kv_cache_expand()
  ...
Warning: memory fragmentation high: free_chunks=12 total_free=2.6 GiB largest_free=512 MiB
```
jordan: this screams fragmentation + aggressive prefetch. Two quick knobs: reduce the default max_new_tokens to 512 for verne32b-int4, and set `prefetch: false` in runtime config for the canary. Also try kv_trim during generation (trim older KV entries when hitting a threshold).
ashley: ran a short canary with those changes (max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=false, kv_trim=true). OOMs disappeared on first pass, but p50 latency went up ~12ms and tail p99 moved ~40ms. Throughput slightly down.
mika: interesting — paste of the successful warmup trace now shows many small freed segments between allocations. Fragmentation warnings persist but no OOM. Perf summary:
- batch=4, max_new=512: p50=86ms (was 74ms), p99=620ms (was 580ms)
- memory: steady allocated ~68 GiB, reserved ~36 GiB, free ~2.8 GiB
takashi: tradeoff is expected. Another angle: enable `kv_trim_threshold` and set it aggressively (e.g. 0.7) so KV trimming starts before we hit critical fragmentation. Also consider adaptive batching by prompt length to avoid large prompts + large max_new_tokens combos.
jordan: sample config we used:
```
model_config:
  name: verne32b-int4
  max_new_tokens: 512
batching:
  max_batch_size: 4
  max_total_tokens: 2048
runtime:
  prefetch: false
  kv_trim: true
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.7
```
ashley: added an adaptive policy in the canary: `policy: len_based` where requests with prompt_len>1024 go to batch_size=1. That eliminated the p99 spikes from huge prompts; p99 back down ~605ms. Will run a full eval overnight vs baseline.
mika: another observation: allocator shows many cudaMalloc/cudaFree calls during warmup which correlates with fragmentation. Is it feasible to flip to cudaMallocAsync caching or to force allocator to hold onto bigger blocks for int4 workloads?
takashi: we can try two low-risk experiments:
1) Enable cudaMallocAsync (if driver supports) to reduce fragmentation from many small frees.
2) After warmup, call `allocator.clear_cached_allocations()` in the runtime to consolidate (we already have a hook for post-warmup).
Patch idea (quick):
```
if (driver_supports_malloc_async) {
  allocator.enable_malloc_async = true
} else {
  // fall back: post-warmup compact
  runtime.post_warmup_hook = allocator.compact()
}
```
infra-bot: canary update: verne32b-int4 c-1845123456 deployed to 3 nodes with config overrides (max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=false)
jordan: also try reducing default max_new_tokens at the API layer for hosted users until we feel comfortable (e.g., lower quota per call). This avoids noisy tenants hitting fragmentation.
ashley: I'll run the overnight suite: baseline (max_new=1024, prefetch=true) vs canary (512,false,kv_trim=0.7,len_based). Will post results tomorrow AM.
mika: summary/action items:
- ashley: run full eval overnight and share numbers (throughput/latency/ooms)
- takashi: try allocator malloc_async toggle + post-warmup compaction patch in a dev branch
- jordan: prepare a low-risk API default change for hosted that can be toggled
- infra-bot: keep canary ~24h and surface any OOM regressions
mika: thanks all — biggest win so far is that OOMs stopped with the config changes. We need to balance that with latency; will iterate on allocator and batching policies.
